exceptions.justification: `repo-contract explain` loads the project's TypeScript config through the project's own tsx: it resolves the constant name "tsx/esm/api" from the project with createRequire(<dir>/package.json) and imports the resolved file URL. Only that one constant name is resolved; nothing computed from input picks the module. Accepted as a risk: a module is loaded at run time, bounded to one constant name. bin/ is the one place ADR 0011 lets load or start anything at run time; the AmbientCapabilities check keeps dist/ free of it.
exceptions.alternatives: A static `import "tsx/esm/api"` would make tsx a runtime dependency of repo-contract and load repo-contract's copy, not the project's. Asking the user to run the config through tsx themselves would move the same load into their shell.
exceptions.remediation: Remove when explain can read a config without executing TypeScript, or when Node can import TypeScript configs natively in every supported version.

exceptions.justification: Imports the file URL that createRequire resolved for the constant name "@stryker-mutator/instrumenter" (see the record for line 6). Only that constant name reaches this import. Accepted as a risk: a module is loaded at run time, bounded to one constant name. bin/ is the one place ADR 0011 lets load or start anything at run time; the AmbientCapabilities check keeps dist/ free of it.
exceptions.alternatives: As for line 6: a static import would bundle a second instrumenter that can disagree with the project's Stryker.
exceptions.remediation: Remove with the line 6 record, when Stryker's report lists mutant-free files.

exceptions.justification: `repo-contract mutation run` imports the project's own Stryker config file (stryker.config.mjs or the `--config` path) to read its `mutate`, report and temp paths. That file is the project's code, which Stryker itself imports a moment later in the same run. Accepted as a risk: the import executes project code the user already runs. bin/ is the one place ADR 0011 lets load or start anything at run time; the AmbientCapabilities check keeps dist/ free of it.
exceptions.alternatives: Parsing the config as text would miss computed values; asking Stryker for its resolved config needs a second Stryker start per run.
exceptions.remediation: Remove when Stryker exposes its resolved config without running, or when the preset passes the paths it needs as options.

exceptions.justification: `repo-contract mutation run` uses createRequire(<project>/package.json) to resolve the constant name "@stryker-mutator/instrumenter" from the project, so it asks the same instrumenter the project's Stryker runs which files hold no mutant. Only that constant name is resolved. Accepted as a risk: a module is loaded at run time, bounded to one constant name. bin/ is the one place ADR 0011 lets load or start anything at run time; the AmbientCapabilities check keeps dist/ free of it.
exceptions.alternatives: A static import would make the instrumenter a runtime dependency of repo-contract and could disagree with the version the project's @stryker-mutator/core pins. Dropping the check would let a report that skipped a file pass as complete.
exceptions.remediation: Remove when Stryker's report lists files it found no mutant in, so the CLI need not run the instrumenter itself.

exceptions.justification: `repo-contract affected` must run the project's OWN TypeScript (the compiler API it needs is the consumer's, version 6 or earlier), so the CLI resolves the literal module name "typescript" from the project directory with createRequire(<dir>/package.json). The specifier is a constant; nothing computed from input is ever loaded, and the loaded module is a build-time dependency the consumer already installed. Accepted as a risk rather than a false positive: the capability is real (a module is loaded at run time), bounded to one constant name, and reviewed here.
exceptions.alternatives: A static `import "typescript"` would load repo-contract's own copy, or fail when a project has none, instead of the project's compiler; an `import()` of the same literal has the same dynamic-load shape under this scan. Passing the compiler in through the library API (`repo-contract/affected` takes `ts` as an argument) is already how the library avoids this; the CLI is the one place that has to find it.
exceptions.remediation: Remove when TypeScript 7 ships a compiler API and the CLI can import a pinned dependency instead of the project's copy, or when the CLI is folded into a consumer-supplied runner.
